trial_court: Additional District Judge, Delhi, CM(M) 684/2010 & CM.13618/2010
case_name: Mon Mohan Kohli vs Natasha Kohli
acts_cited_auto: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

acts_cited.act: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

facts_of_case: Petitioner was married to respondent on 14.11.1994 and a male child was born out of their wedlock. Petitioner filed petition for grant of divorce under Section 13 (1) (ia) of the Hindu Marriage Act on ground of cruelty which is pending. Meanwhile, petitioner filed another petition for grant of decree of nullity under Section 11 of the Hindu Marriage Act in alternate under section 12(c) of the Hindu Marriage Act for annulment of marriage on ground of fraud.

legal_principles.principle: A thing which is void has no existence in the eye of law.
legal_principles.held: Since in the eye of law the relationship of husband and wife did not exist between the petitioner and Smt. Padi, her subsequent marriage with another person will not attract Section 494, I.P.C.
cited_cases: Smt. Padi & Ors. Vs. Union of India AIR 1963 Himachal Pradesh 16 (V 50 C6)
legal_principles.significance: HIGH — highlights the importance of void marriages

legal_principles.principle: A decree which has been declared as void ab initio could not have any binding effect on a third party who would be affected.
legal_principles.held: Ms.Luthra, contends that the said decree was collusive in nature, barred by law of limitation and even otherwise
legal_principles.significance: MEDIUM — emphasizes the importance of considering the validity of a decree

outcome.final_order: Order dated 17.01.2013 passed by the High Court of Delhi allowing the petition and setting aside the order of the trial court.
